_comment: Edit this file to change what gets tracked. The web app's Settings tab can override chase list, retail prices and risk profile per-browser.

retailReference._comment: Standard US MSRP for formats that have ONE fixed retail price. Leave a format null if its retail varies by product - set those per product in productOverrides instead. When unsure, lower is safer than higher: a too-high retail creates fake buys.

formatScore._comment: 0-10. How well this format has historically held and grown value as a long-term sealed hold. Cases, displays and lots use the score of what's inside.

singles._comment: Singles of your chase Pokemon. budgetMin/budgetMax/sweetSpotMax are what the Singles tab shows by default (you can change them in Settings). trackMin/trackMax are wider so a card drifting just outside your budget keeps its price history.

productOverrides._comment: Per TCGplayer product id: retail (MSRP), release (YYYY-MM-DD) and a note on where it came from. Use this for collection boxes, UPCs and anything in the Miscellaneous group.

setOverrides._comment: Print status per set, by TCGplayer group name (or id). printStatus: "in_print" keeps a set in its print-run phase however old it is, so targets stay tied to retail; "out_of_print" = confirmed (its era has ended); "likely_out_of_print" = inferred (no reprint news, rotated, old stock only) and earns part of the out-of-print bonus. TPCi never announces when printing stops. Leave a set out when unsure: an unverified second-year set gets no Strong buy and no buy above 2x retail. Re-check every few months.
